paragraphs: R’ Yose bar Yasian. (A Tanna of a baraita.)

Menachot 6b says, “To exclude these Tannaim, for it was taught: R’ Yose ben Yasiyin and R’ Yehudah HaNachtim said,” etc. Hyman says that the words “ben Yose” are absent from the Tosefta there and likewise from Dikdukei Soferim.
In Avodah Zarah 42a, R’ Yochanan objects to Resh Lakish: “R’ Yose ben Yasian says: one who found the form of a dragon,” etc.

In his account of Mekhilta, Yitro, tractate BaChodesh, chapter 3, Hyman gives R’ Yose son of Rabbi Assi as Rabbi’s opponent. Hyman says it is possible that it SHOULD READ bar Yasin; the Yalkut there, however, reads R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose.

notes.text: “The words ben Yose are absent” does not correspond cleanly to the name as quoted in the supplied sentence; that wording is preserved as a source question. Yasian/Yasiyin/Yasin and Asi are not silently harmonized.

No new primary scalar was returned. Menachot excludes THESE TANNAIM, plural; Yehudah HaNachtim and all Yasian/Yasiyin/Yasin spellings remain distinct. The source says the words ben Yose are absent although its quoted name already lacks them. The older doubled-name search snippet is only a lead, not a fetched Tosefta or Dikdukei Soferim witness. Yochanan’s objection to Resh Lakish is contextual, not Yehudah. The Mekhilta explicitly writes Rabbi in bar-Rabbi-Assi and for his opponent Rabbi; these full titles remain. Hyman says it is POSSIBLE that it SHOULD READ bar Yasin, beside the separate Yalkut Yishmael reading.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. II, p. 732) and the consulted Menachot 6b both read “R’ Yose ben Yose ben Yasiyin.” The supplied quotation and the consulted Tosefta Menachot 1:9 have the shorter patronymic, with variant spellings. The Menachot text consulted also reads HaNachtom where Hyman gives HaNachtim. The reference to Dikdukei Soferim is Hyman’s report. The consulted Mekhilta, BaChodesh 3, reads R’ Yose son of R’ Yehudah. The notes to Lekach Tov on Exodus 24:9 quote the son-of-Assi reading, and Yalkut Shimoni 279 gives R’ Yishmael son of R’ Yose. Hyman’s bar Yasin remains a suggested correction.
